note: Christian camp near Oak Harbor on the Toussaint River side of Ottawa County, open to the public for camping (no alcohol or recreational drugs). The Oaks lots are smaller and nearest the showers; the Pines lots are larger, on the far side of camp by the abandoned railroad tracks. --Claude
summary: Public can book a night: 'Family-oriented Christian camp open to the public', instant-book on RoverPass, no membership. Confirmed $45/$55 on the operator's page; RoverPass's 2027 nights are cheaper on small lots ($29-45), so fees 45-55 -> 29-55. Added max rig 32, showers/flush toilets, season, RoverPass booking; 30A/water/no sewer/no dump confirmed. Note cleaned.
flags: GATE FACTS: base under $50 either way: $29-45 on RoverPass small lots (2027), $45 Oaks / $55 Pines on the operator's page; Good Sam: not a GS Park (stored false); no gateway within 40 km (Point Pelee 68 km). GOOGLE MAPS: 4.1 from 54 reviews. Presence: operator site live, RoverPass claimed (isBookable). Not a family stay.

PUBLIC ACCESS: no membership or group condition found. Operator's rule is the conduct policy only: 'NO ALCOHOL or RECREATIONAL DRUGS of any type will be allowed at camp'; 'Family-oriented Christian camp open to the public. Alcohol, Drug, quiet hour and pet policies strictly enforced.' Monthly RV rates exist on RoverPass ($225-825) but it sells nights on the same lots; no seasonal-only sign.
PHONE: operator's site, RoverPass and the Good Sam directory give (419) 898-6741; the entry and Google Maps have 419-898-6742. Suggest 419-898-6741.

ENGINE vs PAGE: for 2027 RoverPass offers only rate 8605 on four lots (25-32 ft); 'Large Sites', 'Oaks' and 'Pines' types show on the listing but no 2027 night was on sale on the eight dates read, so the $45/$55 prices couldn't be confirmed on the engine. Lot 7 is 8 ft wide ('good for small RV's or tent'). Engine's type label says '30/50 Amps', its site amenities and the operator's page say 30/20, so electric stays 30.
Pin checked on imagery: at the camp, within ~100 m of the lodge area. Stored not waterfront stands: nothing on the pages claims it; the Toussaint channel is beyond a wooded band.
